findings.text: Folio clearing entry that zeroes every page of the given folio while keeping the fault neighbourhood resident last. It derives an aligned base from the hint and folio size, converts the hint to a page index, clamps a neighbourhood defined by a locality radius to folio bounds, then clears right, left and neighbourhood extents in that order, skipping empty extents.

Contiguous user page clearing helper that processes a range in bounded units with scheduling points. It selects a full-range unit under a preemptible model and a fixed batch otherwise, announces sleepability, yields on each iteration, and clears each subrange through the highpage primitive.

Huge page-table allocation entry that ensures upper levels exist and returns a slot for the requested huge size. It allocates missing upper levels, returns the pud slot for pud-sized requests, otherwise selects a shared pmd slot when sharing is wanted and the pud slot is empty or a private pmd slot, failing with null on allocation failure and enforcing that any present slot holds a huge entry and that non-pud sizes are pmd-sized.

Sharing of a pmd table is permitted only when several independent checks all pass: the pud-aligned span around the address lies inside the requesting area, the area allows sharing and carries private lock state, userfaultfd does not forbid sharing, the candidate and requester agree on pmd index and on flags ignoring lock bits, the candidate span lies inside the candidate area, and the candidate carries private lock state. A build variant disables sharing entirely.

Shared pmd establishment that searches other areas mapped at the same file offset for a shareable table, reuses the first usable source with an elevated table reference, installs it into an empty pud slot under the table lock while accounting the table count, drops the extra reference if the slot raced, and otherwise falls back to a private allocation. A build variant never shares and reports absence.

Huge migration wait entry that inspects the huge slot under its dedicated lock while the area is held, returns promptly when the slot is empty or holds no migration marker, and otherwise releases the area read hold and sleeps on the migration marker while holding only the table lock.

Null-safe userfaultfd capability queries that report asynchronous write-protect and read-write-protect handling. Each area-level query delegates to a context-level check that requires a non-null context and the corresponding feature bit sampled with a single atomic read.

Central fault entry that builds a fault descriptor from area, masked and real addresses, flags, file offset and fault allocation mask, ensures upper table levels exist, and dispatches pud, pmd and pte handling with huge-page, migration, device-private, userfaultfd and NUMA paths.

Fault dispatch proceeds from large to small granularity with retry and fallback. Empty upper slots may attempt huge creation when the area permits the corresponding order for faults; raced upper slots retry; non-present pmd markers divert to device-private or migration waiting; readable huge pmd faults may divert to userfaultfd or NUMA handling or copy-on-write handling; otherwise the fault is marked accessed or treated as spurious, and any uncovered case falls through to the small-page path.

Device-private huge fault handling that requests a retry when entered under area-read mode, validates table stability under the pmd lock, publishes the backing page while clearing the pte slot, and when the folio lock is available holds a reference across an unlock, invokes the device migrate-to-RAM operation, then releases lock and reference.

Accessed-state update rules differ by level. The pud helper acquires its own lock, revalidates the slot, marks young and conditionally dirty, propagates access flags and refreshes the cache only on change, then releases. The pmd helper assumes the caller already holds the lock, revalidates, and reports whether an update occurred.

Huge-pmd userfaultfd read-write-protect resolution with synchronous delegation and asynchronous local resolve. The synchronous case forwards to the generic userfault path; the asynchronous case validates stability under lock, rebuilds protections, drops the userfaultfd marker, marks young, opportunistically restores writability when manual upgrade is wanted and permitted, installs the entry and refreshes the cache.

A pmd may gain writability without a further fault only when the area is writable, the entry is readable, neither soft-dirty nor userfaultfd write tracking needs a fault, and ownership holds: private mappings require a normal anonymous exclusive page while shared mappings require a dirty entry.

Write notification is needed only for shared writable areas and then when any tracking interest exists: filesystem operations requesting first-write callbacks, soft-dirty tracking on non-hugetlb areas, userfaultfd write protection, or a file mapping capable of writeback, unless the area protection transformation already altered the supplied protection.

Huge-pmd NUMA balancing consumes the fault locally after attempting migration. It validates stability under lock, evaluates writability including opportunistic upgrade, classifies the fault for grouping and locality while recording access state, asks policy for a misplaced target, isolates the folio when the destination has capacity, migrates without holding the table lock, and on any failure or absence restores a young entry with writability preserved before accounting the outcome.

Policy-driven misplacement returns no target when the policy disables migration, when interleaved or preferred or local or restricted selections already match the current node or have no usable node, and when migrate-toward-referrer is requested but the current task should not trigger migration; otherwise it returns the computed node and always releases the policy reference.

Misplaced folio preparation rejects executable file folios that may be shared, rejects dirty file folios that cannot move asynchronously, rejects destinations without balanced capacity while optionally waking reclaim under tiering mode, and rejects folios that fail list isolation; success isolates the folio and accounts it as isolated with file versus anonymous distinction.

Clearing covers the full folio exactly once across three disjoint extents with the fault neighbourhood last, and clearing of contiguous pages advances by bounded units until the requested count is consumed. Fault handling guarantees that allocation failure reports out-of-memory, stable huge entries are consumed without falling through, and only explicitly marked fallback or uncovered shapes reach the small-page path.

Shared pmd installation orders a file-mapping read lock outside the address-space table lock, elevates the source table reference before acquiring the table lock, installs only into a still-empty slot, and pairs every early search exit and final return with matching releases of both locks.

Fault and migration paths hold the table lock while validating slot stability and mutate tables only after validation. Device-private and userfaultfd and NUMA pmd paths release on mismatch without mutation; migration waiting keeps the table lock while dropping the area read hold; device-private drops the area read hold before requesting retry; policy target selection requires the table lock to be held by the caller.

Several configurations abort or retry rather than proceed on inconsistency: mismatched huge sizes or present non-huge entries trigger fatal checks, missing write permission with an upgrade attempt triggers a one-time warning and refusal, raced pud or pmd slots retry or return success without action, and failed upper-level allocations report out-of-memory.

The fault descriptor observed carries the area, masked and real addresses, flags, file offset, allocation mask, upper-level slots, sampled original pmd, lock pointer, and resolved page and pte slot, with the page slot used for device-private faults and the pte slot cleared there.

Area state relied upon comprises flags, owning address space, file and mapping, private lock token, page protections, operation vector, fault context for userfaultfd, and start and end bounds used for containment and index translation.

Observed fault and policy markers include entry flags FAULT_FLAG_WRITE and FAULT_FLAG_UNSHARE with area-lock entry FAULT_FLAG_VMA_LOCK, result codes VM_FAULT_OOM and VM_FAULT_FALLBACK with retry VM_FAULT_RETRY, huge orders PUD_ORDER and PMD_ORDER with masks HPAGE_PUD_MASK and HPAGE_PMD_MASK and count HPAGE_PMD_NR, absence marker NUMA_NO_NODE, accounting flags TNF_NO_GROUP and TNF_SHARED with local TNF_FAULT_LOCAL and migration outcomes TNF_MIGRATED and TNF_MIGRATE_FAIL, access-time mask LAST_CPUPID_MASK, policy modes MPOL_INTERLEAVE and MPOL_WEIGHTED_INTERLEAVE with MPOL_PREFERRED and MPOL_LOCAL and MPOL_BIND and MPOL_PREFERRED_MANY, and modifiers MPOL_F_MOF and MPOL_F_MORON.

Observed area and feature markers include permission flags VM_MAYSHARE and VM_SHARED with VM_WRITE and VM_EXEC and lock mask VM_LOCKED_MASK, area state bits VMA_WRITE_BIT and VMA_SHARED_BIT with PFNMAP marker VMA_PFNMAP_BIT, userfaultfd capabilities UFFD_FEATURE_WP_ASYNC and UFFD_FEATURE_RWP_ASYNC with synchronous marker VM_UFFD_RWP, clearing tunables FOLIO_ZERO_LOCALITY_RADIUS and PROCESS_PAGES_NON_PREEMPT_BATCH, and granularity markers PUD_SIZE and PMD_SIZE with PUD_MASK and PAGE_SIZE and PAGE_MASK.
